<local-command-stdout></local-command-stdout>

Okay we need to make a bunch of fixes to the phase 1 implementation of METROPOLIX_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md,

Look at the current code in in patches/Metropolix, then fix the following issues, make a commit and push a PR.

[P1] TRK2 slider updates are effectively broken: config-manager.js expects a track index in update_pitches (config-manager.js (line 57)), but the patch only sends 8 slider values via pak -> prepend update_pitches (Metropolix.maxpat (line 761), Metropolix.maxpat (line 764), Metropolix.maxpat (line 839)). Track Select is unconnected (Metropolix.maxpat (line 767)).

[P1] Stages Length is not implemented in behavior: UI dial exists but has no wiring (Metropolix.maxpat (line 779)), and the only sequence-building helper is dead code (buildPulseSeq) (config-manager.js (line 30)).

[P1] Playback Order is currently inert: menu exists (Metropolix.maxpat (line 770)) but has no patchline, and v8 logic has no playback-order handling beyond init + pitch updates (config-manager.js (line 45), config-manager.js (line 56)).

[P1] Track1 note event logic appears miswired around gate 1: gate-state and pitch-change paths are crossed (Metropolix.maxpat (line 593), Metropolix.maxpat (line 597)). This is likely to cause duplicate or incorrect note trigger behavior.

[P1] Signal→MIDI conversion still depends on snapshot~ 20 in timing-critical areas (Metropolix.maxpat (line 445), Metropolix.maxpat (line 484), Metropolix.maxpat (line 562), Metropolix.maxpat (line 563)). For Metropolix-style gates/ratchets this is too coarse and will not be edge-accurate.

[P2] Several Phase 1 UI requirements are present but not functional: Track Select, Playback Order, Stages Length, and Root Note are orphaned (Metropolix.maxpat (line 767), Metropolix.maxpat (line 770), Metropolix.maxpat (line 779), Metropolix.maxpat (line 785)).

[P2] Stage-position outputs exist from p SequencerCore (numoutlets: 8) but are unused at top-level (Metropolix.maxpat (line 382), Metropolix.maxpat (line 819)). So planned position indicators are not implemented.

[P2] TRK2 output parameter exposure is risky: TRK2 live.dials are nested in p Track2Output (Metropolix.maxpat (line 657), Metropolix.maxpat (line 666), Metropolix.maxpat (line 674)), but root parameter registry only lists top-level objects (Metropolix.maxpat (line 841)). This needs runtime verification in Live.

[P3] live.thisdevice exists but is unconnected (Metropolix.maxpat (line 93)), so device-ready init hooks from the plan are not actually in play.

[P3] Swing semantics may diverge from manual intent: clock gen code comments/logic are written around “odd” handling (Metropolix.maxpat (line 294)), while Metropolix docs describe delaying even pulses.

Layout/subpatcher assessment:

Subpatcher partitioning is directionally good for Max 9: p ClockEngine, p SequencerCore, p Track1Output, p Track2Output, p TransportStop are sensible and mostly left-to-right in flow.
Placement is readable enough in patching view, but functionality gaps dominate; this is more “good skeleton” than a completed Phase 1.

content.content:
1→# Metropolix Max4Live MIDI Device - Implementation Plan (v2)
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→Faithful recreation of the Intellijel Metropolix 8-stage pitch and gate sequencer as a **Max4Live MIDI Effect** targeting **Max 9 / Live 12**. The device outputs MIDI on TRK1 and exposes TRK2 as modulation output parameters for the user to map freely within their Ableton Live project.
     6→
     7→### Hardware → M4L Translation
     8→
     9→The hardware Metropolix operates in the eurorack ecosystem with control voltages. This M4L implementation translates everything into the MIDI and Live parameter domains:
    10→
    11→| Metropolix (Hardware)    | M4L Implementation                                                                                   |
    12→| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    13→| 1V/Oct pitch CV          | MIDI note number (0-127) via `midiout`                                                               |
    14→| Gate CV (0V / 5V)        | MIDI note-on / note-off                                                                              |
    15→| Velocity CV              | MIDI velocity (1-127)                                                                                |
    16→| TRK2 pitch/gate/velocity | Normalized `live.dial` parameters (0.0-1.0) — modulation outputs the user maps to any Live parameter |
    17→| CV Lane output (±5V)     | Normalized `live.dial` parameter (0.0-1.0) — user maps externally                                    |
    18→| MOD OUT A / OUT B (±5V)  | Normalized `live.dial` parameters (0.0-1.0) — user maps externally                                   |
    19→| AUX inputs (±5V)         | `live.dial` parameters (0.0-1.0) — external sources map into these                                   |
    20→| CTRL knobs               | `live.dial` parameters — internal routing + user maps externally                                     |
    21→
    22→**There is no concept of control voltage in this implementation.** All modulation sources and outputs are normalized values (0.0-1.0) exposed as automatable Live parameters.
    23→
    24→### Architecture Constraints
    25→
    26→- **TRK1**: Direct MIDI output via `midiout` (pitch, velocity, gate on/off)
    27→- **TRK2**: Modulation output — pitch, velocity, and gate are exposed as `live.dial` parameters that the user maps to any target in their project. No `live.remote~` takeover of remote parameters. TRK2 runs the same sequencer engine as TRK1 but its output is parameter values, not MIDI notes.
    28→- **Transport**: Syncs to Live's transport via `phasor~ @lock 1` for sample-accurate timing. `plugsync~` for transport state. `transport` object for UI display only.
    29→- **Timing-critical path**: Signal-rate objects only (`phasor~`, `stepcounter~`, `stepdiv~`, `stepfun~`, `gen.codebox~`). **v8 JavaScript is NOT used in the timing-critical path** — it runs only in the low-priority thread. v8 is used for configuration, precomputation, preset management, and UI logic only.
    30→- **MIDI output**: Routed through Max 9's `schedule` object for scheduler-thread timing precision.
    31→- **Loopy Mode**: Explicitly excluded from this implementation.
    32→- **Target**: Max 9 features (v8, array._, gen.codebox~, stepfun~/stepdiv~/stepcounter~, string._) are preferred per CLAUDE.md.
    33→- **Modulation I/O**: All modulation outputs are exposed as `live.dial` parameters for user mapping. **v1 does not use `live.modulate~` internally**; if added later, it is a v2 feature and must use bipolar scaling.
    34→
    35→### v1 Scope
    36→
    37→**Included in v1:**
    38→
    39→- 2 tracks with independent stepping (shared base controls, per-track interpretation)
    40→- 8 stages with all per-stage lanes
    41→- Full gate system (4 types + ratchets)
    42→- Quantizer with 49 factory scales + 20 user scales
    43→- 10 playback orders (Linear, Ping Pong, Pendulum, Random, Shuffle, Brownian, Converge, Diverge, Pedal Point, Hopscotch)
    44→- 4 MOD lanes (independent sequencers)
    45→- 2 CTRL knobs + 3 AUX inputs
    46→- Accumulator (full implementation)
    47→- Slide/portamento (3 types)
    48→- 16 presets (2 banks of 8)
    49→- Tabbed UI faithful to hardware layout
    50→
    51→**Deferred to v2:**
    52→
    53→- Remaining 10 playback orders
    54→- 4 additional MOD lanes (total 8)
    55→- Preset chains
    56→- 64 presets (8 banks of 8)
    57→- 80 additional user scales (total 100)
    58→- Full OUT A/B flexible output types
    59→- Push integration / live.banks
    60→- Preset interpolation
    61→
    62→---
    63→
    64→## Data Model
    65→
    66→Based on the Metropolix "What's Stored Where" hierarchy (manual pp. 134-138).
    67→
    68→### Global Settings (Not Per-Preset)
    69→
    70→| Parameter               | Range                      | Notes                                                        |
    71→| ----------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
    72→| MIDI Channel TRK1       | 1-16                       | Channel for direct MIDI output                               |
    73→| Total Pulses            | — / 1-1024                 | Global pulse length; resets all tracks + MOD lanes when set  |
    74→| Root Note               | C-B                        | Global quantizer root                                        |
    75→| Scale Select            | 0-68                       | Index into scale bank (49 factory + 20 user for v1)          |
    76→| User Scales             | 20 scales (2 banks of 10)  | 12-bit bitmasks                                              |
    77→| Bottom Pitch            | C / Root                   | Whether slider bottom maps to C0 or to the current root note |
    78→| CTRL 1/2 Assignments    | Destination enum           | What the CTRL knobs control                                  |
    79→| AUX X/Y/Z Assignments   | Destination + Attenuverter | External modulation inputs                                   |
    80→| AUX X/Y/Z Attenuverters | -100 to +100               | Bipolar scaling                                              |
    81→
    82→### Shared Stage Controls (x8 stages — shared between TRK1 and TRK2)
    83→
    84→Like the hardware, both tracks share the same 8 base controls. Per-track parameters (Slider Octaves, Slider Direction, overrides) diverge from this shared base.
    85→
    86→| Parameter    | Range                  | Notes                                                                                  |
    87→| ------------ | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    88→| Pitch Slider | 0.0-1.0 (normalized)   | Shared physical slider — per-track interpretation via Slider Octaves, Slider Direction |
    89→| Pulse Count  | 1-8                    | Shared switch — can be overridden per-track via Pulse Count Override                   |
    90→| Gate Type    | Single/Multi/Hold/Rest | Shared switch — can be overridden per-track via Gate Type Override                     |
    91→
    92→### Per-Preset Storage
    93→
    94→#### Per-Track (x2: TRK1, TRK2)
    95→
    96→| Parameter            | Range                                                | Default  | Notes                                                                         |
    97→| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    98→| Direction            | Forward/Reverse                                      | Forward  | Reverses the playback order pattern                                           |
    99→| Transpose            | -60 to +60 semitones                                 | 0        | Chromatic offset (applied AFTER accumulator)                                  |
   100→| Slider Octaves       | 1-4                                                  | 3        | Range of pitch sliders for this track                                         |
   101→| Slider Direction     | Normal/Inverted                                      | Normal   | Flip slider interpretation for this track                                     |
   102→| Pulse Count Override | Switch/1-8                                           | Switch   | Switch = use shared hardware value; 1-8 = force all stages                    |
   103→| Gate Type Override   | Switch/Single/Sngl+Rst/Multi/Multi+Rst/Hold/Hold+Rst | Switch   | Switch = use shared value; +Rst variants preserve REST stages                 |
   104→| Playback Order       | 10 orders (v1 enum)                                  | Linear   | Stage traversal pattern                                                       |
   105→| Stages Length        | 1-8                                                  | 8        | Number of active stages                                                       |
   106→| Pulses Length        | 1-64 or Auto                                         | Auto     | Total pulse count                                                             |
   107→| Stage Offset         | 0-7                                                  | 0        | Starting stage shift                                                          |
   108→| Clock Division       | 1-64                                                 | 1        | Clock divider                                                                 |
   109→| Pulse Count Division | 1-8                                                  | 1        | Combines pulses into longer gates (MULTI mode)                                |
   110→| Swing                | 50-78%                                               | 50       | Delays odd-numbered clock pulses (1-indexed)                                  |
   111→| Slide Type           | Analog/Tempo/Acid                                    | Analog   | Portamento behavior                                                           |
   112→| Slide Amount         | 0-100                                                | 0        | Global slide amount                                                           |
   113→| Gate Length          | 1-99% or Hold (100%)                                 | 50%      | Default gate duration                                                         |
   114→| Gate Scale           | (percentage)                                         | 100%     | Scales ALL gate lengths (track + per-stage overrides)                         |
   115→| Gate Stretching      | ON/OFF                                               | OFF      | Changes gate timing reference to full stage duration                          |
   116→| Ratchet Mode         | Multiply/Pulse/Gated                                 | Multiply | Only active when Gate Stretching ON                                           |
   117→| Rest Pitch           | Hold/Update                                          | Hold     | Hold = keep last pitch; Update = use rest stage's slider value                |
   118→| Velocity             | 50/75/100/Track CV                                   | 100      | Fixed options or derived from CV lane                                         |
   119→| Global Reset         | ON/OFF                                               | ON       | Whether track resets on global reset trigger                                  |
   120→| Accumulator Limit+   | 1-28                                                 | 7        | Positive ACCUM boundary (scale degrees)                                       |
   121→| Accumulator Limit-   | 1-28                                                 | 7        | Negative ACCUM boundary (scale degrees)                                       |
   122→| Accumulator Mode     | Stage/Track                                          | Stage    | Stage = per-stage independent accumulators; Track = single shared accumulator |
   123→| Accumulator Order    | Wrap/Pendulum/Random/Hold                            | Wrap     | Behavior at limits                                                            |
   124→| Accumulator Polarity | Unipolar/Bipolar                                     | Unipolar | Uni: 0 to +Limit; Bi: -Limit to +Limit                                        |
   125→| Accumulator Reset    | Manual/Auto/Aux/Mod                                  | Manual   | When ACCUM resets to 0                                                        |
   126→
   127→#### Per-Stage Per-Track (x8 stages x 2 tracks = 16 sets)
   128→
   129→These parameters are independently set per track, per stage:
   130→
   131→| Parameter           | Range               | Notes                                                |
   132→| ------------------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
   133→| Slide Toggle        | ON/OFF              | Enable slide INTO this stage                         |
   134→| Skip                | ON/OFF              | Skip this stage in playback                          |
   135→| Pitch Override      | OFF/C0-C5           | Force specific pitch (replaces slider value)         |
   136→| Gate Override       | OFF/Rest/1-99%/100% | Override track's gate length for this stage          |
   137→| Ratchet Count       | 1-8                 | Subdivisions within pulse                            |
   138→| Probability         | 0-100%              | Chance of stage/pulse firing                         |
   139→| Probability Target  | Stage/Pulse         | Stage = roll once per stage; Pulse = roll each pulse |
   140→| Accumulator Value   | -7 to +7            | Scale degrees to accumulate                          |
   141→| Accumulator Trigger | Stage/Pulse/Ratchet | When ACCUM value is applied                          |
   142→
   143→#### Auxiliary Output Lane (x8 stages per track, x2 tracks)
   144→
   145→The hardware's "CV Lane" — an auxiliary output per track exposed as a mappable parameter.
   146→
   147→| Parameter           | Range                   | Notes                                                     |
   148→| ------------------- | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
   149→| Aux Lane Mode       | Value / Gate Toggle     | Per-track setting                                         |
   150→| Aux Lane Value      | 0.0 to 1.0 (normalized) | Per-stage value                                           |
   151→| Aux Lane Transition | Step/sRamp/pRamp        | Per-stage — how the value interpolates                    |
   152→| Gate Toggle         | ON/OFF                  | Per-stage, when in Gate Toggle mode (1.0 = ON, 0.0 = OFF) |
   153→
   154→#### MOD Lanes (x4 for v1, each with 8 stages)
   155→
   156→| Parameter             | Range                       | Notes                                                        |
   157→| --------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
   158→| Lane Destination      | Modulation destination enum | What this lane modulates                                     |
   159→| Lane Track Assign     | TRK1 / TRK2 / TRK1+2        | Which track(s) this lane affects                             |
   160→| Lane Direction        | Forward/Reverse             | Reverses the lane's playback order                           |
   161→| Lane Playback Order   | Same 10 orders as v1        | Independent of main tracks                                   |
   162→| Lane Length           | 1-8                         | Independent stage count                                      |
   163→| Lane Clock Division   | 1-64                        | Independent clock div                                        |
   164→| Lane Mute             | ON/OFF                      | Mute this lane's output                                      |
   165→| Per-Stage Value       | -100 to +100 (bipolar)      | Modulation amount                                            |
   166→| Per-Stage Ramp Toggle | Step/Ramp                   | Step = instant jump; Ramp = smooth glide over stage duration |
   167→
   168→### Modulation Destination Enum (Shared by MOD/CTRL/AUX)
   169→
   170→Destinations marked ⎍ are trigger/gate-type: positive value = ON, zero/negative = OFF.
   171→
   172→```
   173→None, Accumulate⎍, Accum Rev⎍, Accum Invert⎍, Accum Mode⎍, Accum Polar⎍,
   174→Accum Reset⎍, Clock In Div, Direction⎍, Gate Length, Gate Scale,
   175→Mute⎍, Octave, Pitch Offset, Pitch Post, Pitch Pre, Play Order,
   176→Probability, Pulse Count, Pulse Div, Pulses Len, Ratchet, Reset⎍,
   177→Root, Scale(User), Skip Invert⎍, Slide⎍, Slide Amount, Slider Invert⎍,
   178→Slider Range, Stages Len, Stage Offset, Swing, Velocity
   179→```
   180→
   181→For MOD lanes, two additional output destinations:
   182→
   183→- **OUT A** — exposed as a `live.dial` parameter (0.0-1.0), user maps externally
   184→- **OUT B** — exposed as a `live.dial` parameter (0.0-1.0), user maps externally
   185→
   186→### Modulation Summing Rules
   187→
   188→When multiple sources target the same destination:
   189→
   190→- **CTRL knobs REPLACE** the base value (they don't add to it)
   191→- **AUX inputs ADD** an offset to the current value
   192→- **MOD lanes ADD** an offset to the current value
   193→- Formula: `final_value = (CTRL_value OR base_value) + sum(AUX_offsets) + sum(MOD_offsets)`
   194→- Result clamped to destination's valid range
   195→- Trigger-type (⎍) destinations: OR logic (any positive source activates)
   196→
   197→### Pitch Pipeline (Corrected)
   198→
   199→The pitch pipeline follows the manual's 10-step process exactly:
   200→
   201→```
   202→1. Pitch Slider Position (shared, 0.0-1.0)
   203→   → Interpret via track's Slider Octaves, Slider Direction, Bottom Pitch setting
   204→   → Result: raw semitone offset from bottom of range
   205→
   206→2. Pitch Override (per-stage per-track)
   207→   → If active: REPLACES the slider value entirely
   208→
   209→3. Pitch Pre modulation (from MOD/AUX/CTRL targeting "Pitch Pre")
   210→   → Added BEFORE quantization (chromatic offset)
   211→
   212→4. Accumulator (per-stage or per-track, in scale degrees)
   213→   → Converted to semitones via current scale's degree-to-semitone mapping
   214→   → Added to pitch
   215→
   216→5. Track Transpose (per-track, ±60 chromatic semitones)
   217→   → Added to pitch
   218→
   219→6. Quantization (snap to current scale + root)
   220→   → Nearest scale degree, prefer rounding down on ties
   221→
   222→7. Pitch Post modulation (from MOD/AUX/CTRL targeting "Pitch Post")
   223→   → Added AFTER quantization (chromatic, snapped to semitones)
   224→
   225→8. Pitch Offset modulation (from MOD/AUX/CTRL targeting "Pitch Offset")
   226→   → Added AFTER quantization (continuous/microtonal — for pitch bend output)
   227→
   228→9. Octave modulation (from MOD/AUX/CTRL targeting "Octave")
   229→   → Added in whole octaves (±N * 12 semitones)
   230→
   231→10. Clamp to MIDI range (0-127) → Output
   232→```
   233→
   234→### Accumulator: Gate Type Interaction Table
   235→
   236→The accumulator trigger behavior depends on the stage's gate type:
   237→
   238→| Trigger Setting | HOLD      | MULTI                      | SINGLE                          | REST            |
   239→| --------------- | --------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------- |
   240→| Stage           | Per stage | Per stage                  | Per stage                       | NO accumulation |
   241→| Pulse           | Per stage | Per pulse                  | Per first pulse only            | NO accumulation |
   242→| Ratchet         | Per stage | Per ratchet in every pulse | Per ratchet in first pulse only | NO accumulation |
   243→
   244→**Accumulator Mode clarification:**
   245→
   246→- **Stage mode**: Each stage has its OWN independent accumulator counter. Stage 1's accumulator only increments when stage 1 is visited, and its offset only affects stage 1's pitch. This means 8 independent accumulators per track.
   247→- **Track mode**: ONE shared accumulator for the whole track. Any stage's ACCUM value adds to the shared total, affecting all stages' pitches.
   248→
   249→**Accumulator Order "Random" clarification:**
   250→
   251→- NOT "randomize the total." It's a biased random walk: 50% chance of moving in ACCUM value direction, 30% chance opposite direction, 20% chance no movement. Step size is randomized between 1 and the stage's ACCUM value.
   252→
   253→**Accumulator Reset "Auto" clarification:**
   254→
   255→- Resets whenever the sequence resets, including: manual resets AND automatic resets when fixed PULSES count is reached (Pulses Length ≠ Auto).
   256→

   258→
   259→## Signal-Rate Architecture
   260→
   261→### Why Not v8 for the Sequencer Engine
   262→
   263→**v8 runs ONLY in the low-priority thread.** This means:
   264→
   265→- Extra latency as messages queue between threads (~20ms vs audio buffer latency)
   266→- Timing "slop" / jitter unacceptable for a sequencer
   267→- NOT suitable for clock generation, step advancement, gate timing, or MIDI note output
   268→
   269→### Hybrid Architecture
   270→
   271→```
   272→SIGNAL-RATE LAYER (timing-critical)
   273→├── phasor~ @lock 1          → Master clock (transport-synced sawtooth)
   274→├── stepcounter~              → Pulse counting per stage
   275→├── stepdiv~                  → Variable-length step subdivision
   276→├── stepfun~                  → Pitch/velocity/modulation value lookup
   277→├── gen.codebox~              → Accumulator math, probability, slide, gate generation
   278→├── slide~                    → Portamento processing
   279→└── schedule                  → MIDI output with scheduler-thread precision
   280→
   281→MESSAGE-RATE LAYER (configuration, non-timing-critical)
   282→├── v8 (single instance)      → Scale database init, preset management, UI state,
   283→│                               playback order precomputation, pattern array generation
   284→├── array.*                   → Stage parameter storage and editing
   285→├── dict                      → Track/lane configuration
   286→├── pattrstorage + autopattr  → Preset save/recall
   287→└── live.* UI objects         → User interface
   288→```
   289→
   290→**Key insight**: v8 **precomputes** pattern data (stage index sequences, pitch arrays, gate type arrays), then **pushes** it to signal-rate step objects (`stepfun~ @pattern`, `stepcounter~ @seq`, `stepdiv~ @pattern`). The signal-rate objects handle timing; note quantization still happens in the MIDI-note event path at gate boundaries.
   291→
   292→### Clock Pipeline
   293→
   294→```
   295→[phasor~ 16n @lock 1]                    ← Master clock, transport-synced
   296→    |
   297→[gen.codebox~ ClockDivider]               ← Per-track clock division (1-64)
   298→    |                                       Also handles swing (delays odd pulses)
   299→[stepcounter~ @seq 2 1 3 1 2 1 3 1]      ← Pulse counts per stage
   300→    |                    |
   301→    |              [stage index out]       ← Current stage number
   302→    |
   303→[stepdiv~ @pattern ...]                   ← Subdivide for per-pulse phasors
   304→    |
   305→[gen.codebox~ GateGenerator]              ← Gate width, ratchet subdivision
   306→    |
   307→[schedule] → [midiformat] → [midiout]    ← MIDI output with scheduler precision
   308→```
   309→

   314→### Stage 1: Project Skeleton, Clock Engine, and Minimal UI

   316→**Goal**: Establish the M4L device, signal-rate clock, basic step advancement, and a minimal testable UI.
   317→
   318→#### 1.1 Device Shell
   319→
   320→- Create the `.amxd` project structure with `midiin` / `midiout`
   321→- Set up `live.thisdevice` initialization (Live API calls) + single `loadbang` → `trigger` chain (non-API init)
   322→- Configure `openinpresentation: 1`, grid `[8.0, 8.0]`
   323→- Root subpatcher organization:
   324→  - `[p ClockEngine]` — phasor~, stepcounter~, stepdiv~
   325→  - `[p SequencerCore]` — stepfun~ pitch/gate lookup, gen.codebox~ for processing
   326→  - `[p Track1Output]` — MIDI note output via schedule → midiformat → midiout
   327→  - `[p Track2Output]` — Modulation parameter output
   328→  - `[p ModulationEngine]` — MOD lanes, CTRL, AUX routing

   330→
   331→#### 1.2 Clock Engine (`[p ClockEngine]`)
   332→
   333→- **Master clock**: `phasor~ 16n @lock 1` — signal-rate sawtooth synced to Live transport
   334→- **Transport state**: `plugsync~` outlet 1 for play/stop, outlet 6 for tempo
   335→- **Clock Division** (1-64): `gen.codebox~` divides the master phasor per track
   336→- **Swing** (50-78%): Delays odd-numbered clock pulses (1-indexed). Swing operates on the track's own divided clock, not the master. Implemented in the clock divider gen~ code.
   337→- **Edge detection**: `gen.codebox~` detects phasor resets (falling edges) to generate step triggers
   338→- **Display sync**: `transport` object for bar/beat display in UI only
   339→
   340→#### 1.3 Step Sequencer (Signal Rate)
   341→
   342→- **`stepcounter~`**: Receives clock phasor, advances through pulse counts per stage via `@seq` attribute. Outputs current stage index.
   343→- **`stepdiv~`**: Takes master phasor + stage pulse counts, generates per-step sub-phasors with proportional timing
   344→- **Stage advancement**: stepcounter~ handles the stage/pulse state machine natively
   345→- **Stages Length** (1-8) and **Stage Offset** (0-7): Update stepcounter~ @seq to include only active stages
   346→- **Skip behavior validation spike (required)**: test whether `stepcounter~ @seq` treats `0` as skip. If behavior is unreliable, v8 must precompute sequences with skipped stages removed (no zero-length entries).
   347→- **Skip guard condition**: if all stages are skipped, force one active stage (or hard mute with deterministic idle state) to prevent invalid/empty sequencing state.
   348→- Implement **Linear playback order** only (v8 precomputes the stage index sequence, pushes to stepcounter~)
   349→
   350→#### 1.4 Basic Pitch Output (TRK1 Only)
   351→
   352→- 8 shared pitch sliders (normalized 0.0-1.0)

   356→- Output note-on/note-off via `schedule` → `midiformat` → `midiout`

   359→#### 1.5 Minimal UI

   379→
   380→### Stage 2: Gate System and Note Output
   381→
   382→**Goal**: Full gate type implementation, velocity, and proper note-on/note-off handling.
   383→
   384→#### 2.0 Signal-to-MIDI Bridge (Must Be Explicit)
   385→
   386→The sequencer runs at signal rate, but MIDI output is event-based. The bridge must be deterministic:
   387→
   388→- Detect gate rising/falling edges at signal rate (`edge~` or equivalent gen logic), not via polling.
   389→- On rising edge: sample pitch and velocity atomically, then emit note-on via `schedule` → `midiformat` → `midiout`.
   390→- On falling edge: emit note-off for the currently active note.
   391→- HOLD legato rule: if next note differs, send note-on(new) before note-off(old). If same note, no retrigger.
   392→- Do not use `snapshot~` for TRK1 gate-edge detection.
   393→
   394→#### 2.1 Gate Types
   395→
   396→Implement the 4 gate types per stage:
   397→
   398→- **Single**: Gate fires on the first pulse of the stage only. Remaining pulses produce no gate.
   399→- **Multi**: Gate fires on every pulse. Each pulse gets its own note-on/note-off pair.
   400→- **Hold**: Gate fires on the first pulse and sustains through all pulses. **MIDI legato handling**: when transitioning to next stage with a new pitch, send note-on for new pitch BEFORE note-off for old pitch (overlapping = legato). If same pitch, no re-trigger (true tie). If next stage is REST, note-off fires.
   401→- **Rest**: No gate. Pitch behavior per Rest Pitch setting: **Hold** = keep last played pitch in register; **Update** = pitch register changes to what the rest stage's slider/override would produce (ghost note position, no audible output).
   402→
   403→#### 2.2 Gate Length
   404→
   405→- **Gate Length** parameter: 1-99% or Hold (100%)
   406→  - Percentage of the pulse duration (when Gate Stretching is OFF)
   407→  - 100% / Hold = legato
   408→- **Gate Scale**: multiplier applied to ALL gate lengths — both track gate length AND per-stage gate overrides simultaneously
   409→- **Gate Override** per stage: when not OFF, overrides the track's global gate length for that stage
   410→  - Values: OFF, Rest (no gate), 1-99%, 100%
   411→
   412→#### 2.3 Gate Stretching
   413→
   414→When Gate Stretching is ON:
   415→
   416→- Gate length is calculated relative to the **entire stage duration** (all pulses combined)
   417→- Gates cannot extend beyond stage boundaries; truncate one tick (1/96 of a clock pulse) before the next stage when needed.
   418→- Enables the 3 **Ratchet Modes** (Stage 4)
   419→
   420→#### 2.4 Pulse Count Division
   421→
   422→Per-track, /1 to /8. When Gate Type = MULTI and Pulse Count > 1, determines how many clock pulses are combined into a single gate.
   423→
   424→- Example: MULTI, Pulse Count = 5, Pulse Count Div = /2 → produces three gates (first two are 2 pulses long, third is 1 pulse)
   425→- Affects ratchet timing when Gate Stretching is OFF
   426→
   427→#### 2.5 Velocity
   428→
   429→- Per-track base velocity: fixed options **50 / 75 / 100 / Track CV**
   430→- "Track CV" derives velocity from the auxiliary output lane's per-stage value.
   431→- Stage dependency note: until the aux lane is implemented, stub Track CV to a fixed value (100%) to keep Stage 2 testable.
   432→- Output as MIDI velocity on note-on messages
   433→
   434→**Deliverable**: Full gate type behavior with proper note timing, MIDI legato for HOLD, velocity, gate length, gate scale, pulse count division.
   435→

   437→
   438→### Stage 3: Quantizer and Scale System
   439→
   440→**Goal**: Implement the scale/quantizer system with 49 factory + 20 user scales.
   441→
   442→#### 3.1 Scale Data Structure
   443→
   444→Each scale is a **12-bit bitmask** (C=bit0, C#=bit1, ... B=bit11). `1` = in scale, `0` = not in scale.
   445→
   446→v8 initializes the scale database at device load time and prepares lookup tables for fast note-event quantization.
   447→
   448→#### 3.2 Factory Scale Banks (7 banks of 7 = 49 scales)
   449→
   450→1. **Major Modes** (7): Ionian, Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Aeolian, Locrian
   451→2. **Melodic Minor Modes** (7): Melodic Minor, Dorian b2, Lydian Augmented, Lydian Dominant, Mixolydian b6, Locrian #2, Altered
   452→3. **Harmonic Minor Modes** (7): Harmonic Minor, Locrian #6, Ionian #5, Dorian #4, Phrygian Dominant, Lydian #2, Ultralocrian
   453→4. **Miscellaneous** (7): Major Pentatonic, Minor Pentatonic, Whole Tone, WH Diminished, HW Diminished, Minor Blues, Chromatic
   454→5. **World** (7): Bhairav/Arabic, Hungarian Minor, Chinese, Hirajoshi, In-Sen, Kumoi, Pelog
   455→6. **Major Chords** (7): Major, Maj6, Maj7, Maj7b5, Maj7#5, Dom7, Maj9
   456→7. **Minor Chords** (7): Minor, Min6, Min7, Min7b5, Dim7, Min9, Min11
   457→
   458→**User Scales** (v1): 20 scales (2 banks of 10), each a 12-bit bitmask, user-editable.
   459→
   460→Scale bitmasks are defined using interval arrays (e.g., Major = `[0,2,4,5,7,9,11]`) and computed to bitmasks programmatically by v8 at init time. Do NOT hardcode bitmask decimals.
   461→
   462→#### 3.3 Quantizer Algorithm
   463→
   464→Quantization runs in the MIDI note-event path (at gate note-on time), not as continuous signal quantization:
   465→
   466→1. Compute `pitchClass = (note - root) mod 12`
   467→2. If scale bit is set, pass through
   468→3. If not, find nearest set bit (check ±1, ±2, etc.; prefer rounding down on ties)
   469→4. Reconstruct: `octave * 12 + root + quantized_pitchClass`
   470→
   471→#### 3.4 Integration
   472→
   473→The quantizer is step 6 in the 10-step pitch pipeline (see Data Model section).
   474→
   475→**Deliverable**: Working quantizer with 69 scales (49 factory + 20 user), root note selection, integrated into pitch pipeline.
   476→

   478→
   479→### Stage 4: Playback Orders and Ratcheting
   480→
   481→**Goal**: Implement 10 playback orders and ratchet subdivisions.
   482→
   483→#### 4.1 Playback Order Engine
   484→
   485→v8 precomputes the full stage index sequence for the selected order + length + offset, then pushes the sequence array to `stepcounter~` and `stepfun~`. When the order or length changes, v8 recomputes and queues a pattern update.
   486→
   487→Pattern updates must be applied on a reset boundary (or with `@syncupdate` set to reset/sequence-end modes) to avoid mid-cycle glitches.
   488→
   489→Each track also has a **Direction** parameter (Forward/Reverse) that reverses the computed sequence.
   490→
   491→#### 4.2 v1 Order Implementations (10 orders)
   492→
   493→All sequences below use 1-based stage numbering from the manual. For 8 stages:
   494→
   495→1. **Linear**: 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 (simple forward loop)
   496→2. **Ping Pong**: 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1 (endpoints repeat)
   497→3. **Pendulum**: 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,7,6,5,4,3,2 (endpoints do not repeat)
   498→4. **Random**: Pure random, any stage (can repeat immediately)
   499→5. **Shuffle**: Random permutation of all stages; repeat that same permutation until reset, then reshuffle
   500→6. **Brownian**: 50% forward, 25% stay, 25% backward (3 outcomes, not 2)
   501→7. **Converge**: 1,8,2,7,3,6,4,5 (from outside in)
   502→8. **Diverge**: 4,5,3,6,2,7,1,8 (from inside out)
   503→9. **Pedal Point**: 1,2,1,3,1,4,1,5,1,6,1,7,1,8 (alternates with first stage)
   504→10. **Hopscotch**: 1,3,2,4,3,5,4,6,5,7,6,8,7,1,8,2 (step forward 2, step back 1 — NOT alternating with stage 1)
   505→
   506→**Important**: Use the manual's explicit sequence patterns as source of truth. Do NOT try to derive sequences algorithmically from the order name — hardcode or generate from the manual's examples.
   507→
   508→**v2 orders** (deferred): Odd/Even, Jump by 2/3/4/5, Arp 3 Shift -1, Arp 4 Shift -2, Arp 4 Shift -1, Growing, Shrinking.
   509→
   510→#### 4.3 Ratcheting
   511→
   512→Per-stage ratchet count (1-8). When ratchet > 1, the pulse is subdivided into rapid repeated gates.
   513→
   514→**Gate Stretching OFF**: Ratchets subdivide a single clock pulse into N equal parts. Each sub-gate gets `gate_length%` of the sub-division duration.
   515→
   516→**Gate Stretching ON — Multiply**: Ratchets span the entire stage duration (all pulses). Creates `ratchet_count` gates spread across the stage.
   517→
   518→**Gate Stretching ON — Pulse**: All ratchets play within a single clock pulse. Rate = `ratchet_count` per pulse. Duration fixed to one pulse regardless of gate length.
   519→
   520→**Gate Stretching ON — Gated**: Same rate as Pulse mode but actual gate count depends on gate length. Ratchets fire at the rate but some may be cut off by the gate closing.
   521→
   522→**Ratchet + Pulse Count Div interaction**: When Gate Stretching OFF, MULTI gate, Ratchets=4, Pulse Div=/2 → 4 rapid gates within each combined 2-pulse gate.
   523→
   524→Boundary rule still applies in all ratchet modes: no gate may extend into the next stage.
   525→
   526→Implementation: `gen.codebox~` subdivides the per-step phasor from `stepdiv~` into ratchet sub-phasors, generating sub-gate on/off events.
   527→
   528→**Deliverable**: 10 playback orders with direction, ratcheting with all modes and pulse count div interaction.

   531→
   532→### Stage 5: Slide/Portamento and Per-Stage Lanes
   533→
   534→**Goal**: Implement slide and all per-stage lane parameters.
   535→
   536→#### 5.1 Slide (Portamento)
   537→
   538→Per-stage slide toggle + per-track slide amount (0-100) and slide type.
   539→
   540→Three slide types:
   541→
   542→- **Analog**: Constant-time glide. `slide~` object with fixed slide rate (independent of tempo).
   543→- **Tempo**: Tempo-synced glide. Slide rate scales with BPM so it feels the same at any tempo. Use `gen.codebox~` with tempo-derived coefficient.
   544→- **Acid**: Slide at the **start of the next stage**. Previous note's gate is held through the transition (legato into glide). Emulates TB-303 slide.
   545→
   546→For MIDI: use **pitch bend** messages for smooth glide. `gen.codebox~` or `slide~` generates the glide curve, output is quantized to 14-bit pitch bend values via `midiformat` inlet 4. Document expected pitch bend range (±2 semitones default; larger intervals require the receiving instrument to be configured).
   547→
   548→Pitch-bend constraint: bend is channel-wide. Keep each track monophonic per MIDI channel and order note-off/note-on transitions accordingly so unrelated notes are not bent.
   549→
   550→#### 5.2 Probability
   551→
   552→- Per-stage probability (0-100%)
   553→- **Stage target**: Roll once when entering stage; fail = entire stage treated as Rest
   554→- **Pulse target**: Roll each pulse independently; fail = that pulse treated as Rest
   555→- Implemented in `gen.codebox~` using a noise source seeded per step
   556→
   557→#### 5.3 Pitch Override
   558→
   559→- Per-stage per-track, OFF or specific MIDI note (C0-C5)
   560→- Replaces the slider value at step 2 of the pitch pipeline
   561→- Still goes through Pitch Pre, Accumulator, Transpose, Quantize, Pitch Post, Pitch Offset, Octave
   562→
   563→#### 5.4 Gate Override
   564→
   565→- Per-stage per-track, OFF / Rest / 1-99% / 100%
   566→- Overrides track's gate length for this stage (but Gate Scale still applies on top)
   567→
   568→#### 5.5 Accumulator
   569→
   570→See Data Model section for the full specification including:
   571→
   572→- Stage mode (8 independent accumulators per track) vs Track mode (1 shared)
   573→- Gate type interaction table
   574→- Random order: biased random walk (50/30/20 split)
   575→- Auto reset: triggers on sequence reset AND when fixed Pulses Length is reached
   576→- Diatonic interval conversion via precomputed scale-degree-to-semitone lookup table
   577→
   578→Implementation: `gen.codebox~` for the accumulator state machine. The scale-degree-to-semitone table is precomputed by v8 whenever scale/root changes, pushed to a gen~ `data` buffer.
   579→
   580→**Deliverable**: Slide with 3 types, probability, pitch/gate overrides, full accumulator with all modes.

   583→
   584→### Stage 6: Track 2 Modulation Output
   585→
   586→**Goal**: Set up TRK2 as modulation output.
   587→
   588→#### 6.1 TRK2 Architecture
   589→
   590→TRK2 runs the same sequencer engine as TRK1 (shared pitch sliders with independent per-track interpretation). The critical difference: TRK2 does NOT output MIDI notes. Instead, its pitch, velocity, and gate values are exposed as **`live.dial` parameters** on the device.
   591→
   592→| TRK2 Output   | Parameter Type                     | Range      | Notes                                                |
   593→| ------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
   594→| TRK2 Pitch    | `live.dial` (Automated and Stored) | 0.0-1.0    | Normalized pitch value, user maps to any destination |
   595→| TRK2 Velocity | `live.dial` (Automated and Stored) | 0.0-1.0    | Normalized velocity                                  |
   596→| TRK2 Gate     | `live.dial` (Automated and Stored) | 0.0 or 1.0 | Gate on/off                                          |
   597→
   598→The user maps these parameters to any target in their Live project using Live's parameter mapping, MIDI mapping, or other M4L devices.
   599→
   600→#### 6.2 Why Not live.remote~
   601→
   602→`live.remote~` **takes over** the target parameter — the user loses manual control and the modulation ring disappears. For a sequencer output that the user wants to combine with their own adjustments, this is poor UX. Instead:
   603→
   604→- TRK2 outputs are simple `live.dial` parameters the user can map themselves
   605→- For users who want `live.modulate~`-style offset behavior (modulation ring, doesn't take over), they can use an LFO-style M4L routing device or we can add `live.modulate~` support in v2
   606→- This approach is simpler, more flexible, and doesn't require Live API path resolution at init time
   607→
   608→#### 6.3 Signal Path
   609→
   610→```
   611→Sequencer Engine (TRK2, signal-rate)
   612→  → gen.codebox~ (converts pitch/vel/gate to normalized 0.0-1.0)
   613→  → snapshot~ 30 (sample signal to message rate)
   614→  → speedlim 5 (limit update rate)
   615→  → live.dial parameters (TRK2 Pitch, TRK2 Velocity, TRK2 Gate)
   616→```
   617→
   618→No `line~` smoothing for pitch (we want discrete steps, not glides — unless slide is active). Gate should be immediate (0 or 1).
   619→
   620→**Deliverable**: TRK2 running same engine as TRK1, outputting to mappable `live.dial` parameters.
   621→

   623→
   624→### Stage 7: Modulation System (MOD Lanes, CTRL, AUX)
   625→
   626→**Goal**: Implement 4 MOD lanes, 2 CTRL knobs, and 3 AUX inputs.
   627→
   628→#### 7.1 MOD Lanes (4 for v1)
   629→
   630→Each MOD lane is an independent mini-sequencer:
   631→
   632→- **8 stage values** (-100 to +100, bipolar)
   633→- **Per-stage ramp toggle** (Step = instant jump, Ramp = smooth glide over stage duration)
   634→- **Independent Playback Order** (same 10 v1 orders)
   635→- **Independent Direction** (Forward/Reverse)
   636→- **Independent Length** (1-8 stages)
   637→- **Independent Clock Division** (1-64)
   638→- **Track Assignment** (TRK1 / TRK2 / TRK1+2)
   639→- **Mute** toggle per lane
   640→- **Destination** from the modulation destination enum
   641→
   642→MOD lanes use the same `phasor~` + `stepfun~` architecture as the main tracks, with their own clock division derived from the master clock. v8 precomputes the stage value patterns; signal-rate objects handle timing.
   643→
   644→#### 7.2 CTRL Knobs
   645→
   646→2 assignable `live.dial` objects (Automated and Stored):
   647→
   648→- Each assigned to one destination from the modulation destination enum
   649→- **CTRL REPLACES** the base value (does not add to it)
   650→- When a CTRL knob targets a destination, its value becomes the new base; MOD/AUX offsets apply on top
   651→
   652→#### 7.3 AUX Inputs
   653→
   654→3 `live.dial` parameters (X, Y, Z) — Automated and Stored:
   655→
   656→- External controllers, LFOs, other M4L devices, or Live automation drive these
   657→- 0.0-1.0 range; 0.5 = center / no modulation
   658→- Each has Destination (enum) + Attenuverter (-100 to +100)
   659→- Internal value = `(AUX - 0.5) * 2 * (attenuverter / 100)` — centered bipolar
   660→- **AUX ADDS** an offset (does not replace)
   661→- For gate-type destinations: attenuverter alone (even without external input) can activate the gate if moved from center
   662→
   663→#### 7.4 Modulation Bus Implementation
   664→
   665→- Central `[p ModulationBus]` collects values from all sources
   666→- Routes summed/replaced values to target parameters
   667→- Hybrid routing:
   668→  - Signal-rate direct paths for timing-critical destinations (clock/gate/pulse/ratchet-related)
   669→  - Message-rate paths for UI/state and non-timing-critical parameters

   727→#### 9.1 pattrstorage Architecture
   728→
   729→- Single `pattrstorage` at root level — no nesting

  1031→## Appendix E: Critical Implementation Notes
  1032→
  1033→### 1. Timing Architecture
  1034→
  1035→- **Clock**: `phasor~ 16n @lock 1` for master clock (signal-rate, transport-synced)
  1036→- **Step objects**: `stepcounter~`, `stepdiv~`, `stepfun~` for step sequencing (signal-rate)
  1037→- **Custom logic**: `gen.codebox~` for accumulator, probability, gate generation, slide
  1038→- **Signal→MIDI bridge**: edge-based gate detection at signal rate, then event emission through `schedule`
  1039→- **MIDI output**: Route through `schedule` object for scheduler-thread timing precision
  1040→- **UI display**: `transport` object for bar/beat display (NOT for timing)
  1041→- `plugsync~` for transport state (play/stop) and tempo reading
  1042→- Swing and ratchet timing is sub-millisecond accurate via signal-rate processing
  1043→- `phasor~ @lock 1` must use notevalue rates; implement clock division downstream
  1044→- Use step-object sync-update settings (or reset-boundary apply) to avoid mid-cycle pattern glitches
  1045→
  1046→### 2. v8 JavaScript — Configuration Only
  1047→
  1048→v8 runs in the low-priority thread. **Never use v8 in the timing-critical path.** Use v8 for:
  1049→
  1050→- Scale database initialization (interval arrays → bitmasks → event-quantizer lookup tables)
  1051→- Playback order precomputation (generate stage index sequences → push to stepfun~ @pattern, stepcounter~ @seq)
  1052→- Preset save/load orchestration
  1053→- UI state management (track selection, stage selection, tab navigation)
  1054→- Parameter validation and formatting
  1055→- Single `v8` instance (`config-manager.js`) to minimize thread-switching overhead
  1056→
  1057→### 3. State Management
  1058→
  1059→- ~383 parameters + runtime state
  1060→- Runtime state (positions, counters, accumulator totals) is Hidden / not saved in presets
  1061→- On transport stop: `flush` all notes, reset modulation outputs, reset MOD lanes, optionally reset accumulators (if Reset = Auto)
  1062→- On transport start: reset to beginning of sequence
  1063→- On preset change: flush + state reset (see Stage 9.4)
  1064→
  1065→### 4. MIDI Thru
  1066→
  1067→All MIDI entering via `midiin` must be forwarded to `midiout` unless intentionally filtered. The sequencer generates its own MIDI; incoming MIDI passes through.
  1068→
  1069→### 5. No Control Voltage — Everything is Parameters
  1070→
  1071→All modulation outputs are normalized `live.dial` parameters (0.0-1.0). All modulation inputs (AUX X/Y/Z) are `live.dial` parameters that any automation or external source can drive. The user maps these freely within their Live project.
  1072→
  1073→### 6. pattrstorage Best Practices
  1074→
  1075→- Single instance at root level, no nesting
  1076→- `autopattr` to auto-register all named live.\* objects
  1077→- `changemode 1` — only transmit changed values on recall
  1078→- `priority` message to sequence load order
  1079→- "Parameter Mode Enable" to store within Live set
  1080→- Keep Automated and Stored count to ~33 (Tier 1 only)
  1081→
  1082→### 7. Scale Change Mid-Sequence
  1083→
  1084→When scale changes during playback:
  1085→
  1086→- Current pitch values are re-quantized to the new scale
  1087→- Accumulator state persists (still counting in scale degrees, but degree-to-semitone mapping changes)
  1088→- v8 recomputes the scale-degree-to-semitone lookup table used by the note-event quantizer

   504→def get_object_name(box: dict) -> str:
   505→    maxclass = box.get("maxclass", "")
   506→    if maxclass == "newobj":
   507→        text = box.get("text", "")
   508→        if text:
   509→            return text.split()[0]
   510→        return ""
   511→    return maxclass
   512→
   513→
   514→def get_object_args(box: dict) -> List[str]:
   515→    text = box.get("text", "")
   516→    if not text:
   517→        return []
   518→    parts = text.split()
   519→    if len(parts) <= 1:
   520→        return []
   521→    args = []
   522→    for p in parts[1:]:
   523→        if p.startswith("@"):
   524→            break
   525→        args.append(p)
   526→    return args
   527→
   528→
   529→def resolve_object_info(box: dict) -> Optional[ObjectInfo]:
   530→    maxclass = box.get("maxclass", "")
   531→    if maxclass != "newobj":
   532→        return MAXCLASS_DEFAULTS.get(maxclass)
   533→    name = get_object_name(box)
   534→    if not name:
   535→        return None
   536→    if name in DYNAMIC_RESOLVERS:
   537→        args = get_object_args(box)
   538→        return DYNAMIC_RESOLVERS[name](args)
   539→    info = KNOWN_OBJECTS.get(name)
   540→    return info

   543→def _detect_m4l(patcher: dict, filepath: str = "") -> bool:

   545→    if filepath.endswith(".amxd"):

   551→        maxclass = box.get("maxclass", "")
   552→        if name in indicators or maxclass.startswith("live."):

   838→def check_message_domain_cycles(
   839→    boxes: List[dict], lines: List[dict], patcher_path: str
   840→) -> List[Diagnostic]:
   841→    """Detect cycles in the message-rate connection graph."""
   842→    diags: List[Diagnostic] = []
   843→    box_map = {box.get("id"): box for box in boxes}
   844→
   845→    # Build adjacency list for message-domain connections only
   846→    adj: Dict[str, set] = defaultdict(set)
   847→    for line in lines:
   848→        src = line.get("source", [])
   849→        dst = line.get("destination", [])
   850→        if len(src) < 2 or len(dst) < 2:
   851→            continue
   852→        src_id, outlet_idx = src[0], src[1]
   853→        dst_id = dst[0]
   854→        src_box = box_map.get(src_id)
   855→        if src_box is None:
   856→            continue
   857→        # Skip signal-rate connections
   858→        outlettype = src_box.get("outlettype", [])
   859→        if outlet_idx < len(outlettype) and outlettype[outlet_idx] == "signal":
   860→            continue
   861→        # Skip outgoing edges from async-break objects
   862→        src_name = get_object_name(src_box)
   863→        if src_name in ASYNC_BREAK_OBJECTS:
   864→            continue
   865→        adj[src_id].add(dst_id)
   866→
   867→    # Collect all nodes
   868→    all_nodes = set(adj.keys())
   869→    for targets in adj.values():
   870→        all_nodes.update(targets)
   871→
   872→    # Iterative DFS for back-edge (cycle) detection
   873→    WHITE, GRAY, BLACK = 0, 1, 2
   874→    color: Dict[str, int] = {}
   875→    reported: set = set()
   876→
   877→    for start in sorted(all_nodes):
   878→        if color.get(start, WHITE) != WHITE:
   879→            continue
   880→        stack = [(start, iter(sorted(adj.get(start, set()))))]
   881→        path = [start]
   882→        color[start] = GRAY
   883→
   884→        while stack:
   885→            _node, children_iter = stack[-1]
   886→            advanced = False
   887→            for child in children_iter:
   888→                if color.get(child, WHITE) == GRAY:
   889→                    idx = path.index(child)
   890→                    cycle_key = tuple(sorted(path[idx:]))
   891→                    if cycle_key not in reported:
   892→                        reported.add(cycle_key)
   893→                        cycle_str = " \u2192 ".join(path[idx:] + [child])
   894→                        diags.append(Diagnostic(
   895→                            "warning", patcher_path, "",
   896→                            f"message-domain cycle: {cycle_str}"
   897→                        ))
   898→                elif color.get(child, WHITE) == WHITE:
   899→                    color[child] = GRAY
   900→                    path.append(child)
   901→                    stack.append(
   902→                        (child, iter(sorted(adj.get(child, set()))))
   903→                    )
   904→                    advanced = True
   905→                    break
   906→            if not advanced:
   907→                color[stack[-1][0]] = BLACK
   908→                path.pop()
   909→                stack.pop()
   910→
   911→    return diags

  1025→def check_self_connection(

  1032→        src = line.get("source", [])

  1035→            continue
  1036→        if src[0] != dst[0]:
  1037→            continue
  1038→        # Self-connections in signal domain are valid (feedback)
  1039→        src_box = box_map.get(src[0])

  1044→            continue

  1056→def check_tapin_tapout_connection(
  1057→    boxes: List[dict], lines: List[dict], patcher_path: str
  1058→) -> List[Diagnostic]:
  1059→    """Error when tapin~ is not directly connected to tapout~."""
  1060→    diags: List[Diagnostic] = []
  1061→    box_map = {box.get("id"): box for box in boxes}
  1062→    tapin_ids = {
  1063→        box.get("id") for box in boxes
  1064→        if get_object_name(box) == "tapin~"
  1065→    }
  1066→    tapout_ids = {
  1067→        box.get("id") for box in boxes
  1068→        if get_object_name(box) == "tapout~"
  1069→    }
  1070→    if not tapin_ids or not tapout_ids:
  1071→        return diags
  1072→
  1073→    # Build direct adjacency from tapin~
  1074→    tapin_targets: Dict[str, set] = defaultdict(set)
  1075→    for line in lines:
  1076→        src = line.get("source", [])
  1077→        dst = line.get("destination", [])
  1078→        if len(src) >= 1 and src[0] in tapin_ids:
  1079→            if len(dst) >= 1:
  1080→                tapin_targets[src[0]].add(dst[0])
  1081→
  1082→    for tapin_id in tapin_ids:
  1083→        targets = tapin_targets.get(tapin_id, set())
  1084→        tapout_connected = targets & tapout_ids
  1085→        non_tapout = targets - tapout_ids
  1086→        if not tapout_connected:
  1087→            diags.append(Diagnostic(
  1088→                "error", patcher_path, tapin_id,
  1089→                "tapin~ has no direct connection to tapout~ "
  1090→                "(tapin~ must connect directly to tapout~)"
  1091→            ))
  1092→        if non_tapout:
  1093→            for target_id in non_tapout:
  1094→                target_box = box_map.get(target_id)
  1095→                target_name = get_object_name(target_box) if target_box \
  1096→                    else target_id
  1097→                diags.append(Diagnostic(
  1098→                    "warning", patcher_path, tapin_id,
  1099→                    f"tapin~ connected to '{target_name}' ({target_id}) "
  1100→                    f"instead of tapout~ (objects between tapin~/tapout~ "
  1101→                    f"are not supported)"
  1102→                ))
  1103→    return diags

  1110→def check_subpatcher_port_indices(
  1111→    child_boxes: List[dict], child_path: str, classnamespace: str
  1112→) -> List[Diagnostic]:
  1113→    """Check inlet/outlet indices are contiguous 1-based with no gaps."""
  1114→    diags: List[Diagnostic] = []
  1115→
  1116→    if classnamespace == "dsp.gen":
  1117→        in_indices: List[int] = []
  1118→        out_indices: List[int] = []
  1119→        for box in child_boxes:
  1120→            if box.get("maxclass") != "newobj":
  1121→                continue
  1122→            parts = box.get("text", "").split()
  1123→            if len(parts) >= 2:
  1124→                try:
  1125→                    idx = int(parts[1])
  1126→                except ValueError:
  1127→                    continue
  1128→                if parts[0] == "in":
  1129→                    in_indices.append(idx)
  1130→                elif parts[0] == "out":
  1131→                    out_indices.append(idx)
  1132→    else:
  1133→        in_indices = []
  1134→        out_indices = []
  1135→        for box in child_boxes:
  1136→            mc = box.get("maxclass", "")
  1137→            idx = box.get("index")
  1138→            if idx is None:
  1139→                continue
  1140→            if mc == "inlet":
  1141→                in_indices.append(idx)
  1142→            elif mc == "outlet":
  1143→                out_indices.append(idx)
  1144→
  1145→    for label, indices in [("inlet", in_indices), ("outlet", out_indices)]:
  1146→        if not indices:
  1147→            continue
  1148→        sorted_idx = sorted(indices)
  1149→        expected = list(range(1, max(sorted_idx) + 1))
  1150→        if sorted_idx != expected:
  1151→            missing = sorted(set(expected) - set(sorted_idx))
  1152→            dupes = sorted(i for i, c in Counter(sorted_idx).items() if c > 1)
  1153→            parts = []
  1154→            if missing:
  1155→                parts.append(f"missing: {missing}")
  1156→            if dupes:
  1157→                parts.append(f"duplicates: {dupes}")
  1158→            diags.append(Diagnostic(
  1159→                "error", child_path, "",
  1160→                f"{label} index gap ({'; '.join(parts)})"
  1161→            ))
  1162→    return diags

  1165→def check_subpatcher_port_count(
  1166→    parent_box: dict, child_boxes: List[dict],
  1167→    child_path: str, classnamespace: str
  1168→) -> List[Diagnostic]:
  1169→    """Check parent numinlets/numoutlets matches child port object count."""
  1170→    diags: List[Diagnostic] = []
  1171→    parent_text = parent_box.get("text", "")
  1172→    # Skip poly~/pfft~ — complex parent-child port relationship
  1173→    first_word = parent_text.split()[0] if parent_text else ""
  1174→    if first_word in ("poly~", "pfft~"):
  1175→        return diags
  1176→
  1177→    if classnamespace == "dsp.gen":
  1178→        child_in = sum(
  1179→            1 for b in child_boxes
  1180→            if b.get("maxclass") == "newobj"
  1181→            and b.get("text", "").split()[0] == "in"
  1182→        )
  1183→        child_out = sum(
  1184→            1 for b in child_boxes
  1185→            if b.get("maxclass") == "newobj"
  1186→            and b.get("text", "").split()[0] == "out"
  1187→        )
  1188→    else:
  1189→        child_in = sum(1 for b in child_boxes if b.get("maxclass") == "inlet")
  1190→        child_out = sum(
  1191→            1 for b in child_boxes if b.get("maxclass") == "outlet"
  1192→        )
  1193→
  1194→    parent_in = parent_box.get("numinlets", 0)
  1195→    parent_out = parent_box.get("numoutlets", 0)
  1196→
  1197→    if child_in != parent_in:
  1198→        diags.append(Diagnostic(
  1199→            "error", child_path, "",
  1200→            f"parent declares {parent_in} inlets but subpatcher has "
  1201→            f"{child_in} inlet objects"
  1202→        ))
  1203→    if child_out != parent_out:
  1204→        diags.append(Diagnostic(
  1205→            "error", child_path, "",
  1206→            f"parent declares {parent_out} outlets but subpatcher has "
  1207→            f"{child_out} outlet objects"
  1208→        ))
  1209→    return diags

  1868→def validate_file(filepath: str) -> List[Diagnostic]:

  2012→            tag = "ERROR  "

  2015→            tag = "WARNING"
  2016→        else:

  2018→            tag = "INFO   "
  2019→        loc = d.patcher_path
  2020→        if d.object_id:

Now let me provide you with the complete analysis. Let me compile all the information together:

## Complete Analysis of Metropolix Implementation

Based on my thorough exploration of the patches/Metropolix directory, here's everything you need to understand about the full implementation:

### 1. Directory Structure

```
patches/Metropolix/
├── Metropolix.maxpat          (862 lines, ~67KB JSON)
└── code/
    └── config-manager.js       (65 lines)
```

### 2. config-manager.js - Complete Contents

This file is the v8 JavaScript configuration manager that runs in the low-priority thread:

```javascript
/**
 * Metropolix Config Manager (v8)
 *
 * Runs in the low-priority thread. NOT used for timing-critical operations.
 * Handles: scale database init, playback order precomputation,
 * pitch array generation, UI state management, preset logic.
 */

// Default pitch slider values (normalized 0.0-1.0, center = 0.5)
const DEFAULT_PITCHES = [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5];
const DEFAULT_PULSE_COUNTS = [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1];
const DEFAULT_GATE_TYPES = [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]; // 1 = Single

const SLIDER_OCTAVES_DEFAULT = 3;
const BOTTOM_PITCH_DEFAULT = 36; // C2

/**
 * Convert normalized slider values to MIDI note numbers.
 * note = bottom_pitch + round(slider * sliderOctaves * 12)
 */
function slidersToPitches(sliders, sliderOctaves, bottomPitch) {
	const range = sliderOctaves * 12;
	return sliders.map(s => Math.round(bottomPitch + s * range));
}

/**
 * Generate the pulse count array for stepcounter~ @seq.
 * Applies stages length and stage offset.
 */
function buildPulseSeq(pulseCounts, stagesLength, stageOffset) {
	const seq = [];
	for (let i = 0; i < stagesLength; i++) {
		const idx = (i + stageOffset) % 8;
		seq.push(pulseCounts[idx]);
	}
	return seq;
}

/**
 * Handle incoming messages from the patcher.
 */
function anything() {
	const msg = arrayfromargs(messagename, arguments);

	if (msg[0] === "init") {
		// Send default patterns to sequencer objects
		const pitches = slidersToPitches(DEFAULT_PITCHES, SLIDER_OCTAVES_DEFAULT, BOTTOM_PITCH_DEFAULT);
		outlet(0, "pitches_trk1", ...pitches);
		outlet(0, "pitches_trk2", ...pitches);
		outlet(0, "pulses_trk1", ...DEFAULT_PULSE_COUNTS);
		outlet(0, "pulses_trk2", ...DEFAULT_PULSE_COUNTS);
		outlet(0, "gatetypes_trk1", ...DEFAULT_GATE_TYPES);
		outlet(0, "gatetypes_trk2", ...DEFAULT_GATE_TYPES);
	}

	if (msg[0] === "update_pitches") {
		// msg[1..8] = slider values, msg[9] = track (0=TRK1, 1=TRK2)
		const sliders = msg.slice(1, 9).map(Number);
		const track = Number(msg[9]) || 0;
		const pitches = slidersToPitches(sliders, SLIDER_OCTAVES_DEFAULT, BOTTOM_PITCH_DEFAULT);
		const prefix = track === 0 ? "pitches_trk1" : "pitches_trk2";
		outlet(0, prefix, ...pitches);
	}
}
```

**Key Points:**
- Very minimal v8 implementation (only 65 lines)
- Handles default initialization of pitches, pulse counts, and gate types
- Converts normalized slider values (0.0-1.0) to MIDI note numbers
- Builds pulse sequences for stepcounter~
- Runs in low-priority thread (not timing-critical)

### 3. Metropolix.maxpat - Structure Overview

The patch is 862 lines of JSON (66KB). **Complete file available at:**
`/Users/user1303836/.REDACTED.txt`

Key structure:
- **Target**: Max 9 / Live 12
- **Device Type**: MIDI Effect (has `midiin` and `midiout`)
- **Window**: 750x600 pixels
- **Presentation Mode**: Enabled (`openinpresentation: 1`)
- **Grid**: 8.0 x 8.0 (root patch standard)
- **Objects Count**: ~40-50 boxes (from initial structure)
- **Description**: "Metropolix - 8-stage pitch and gate sequencer inspired by Intellijel Metropolix"

### 4. METROPOLIX_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md - Complete Contents

This is a comprehensive 1089-line specification document located at:
`REDACTED.md`

**Complete contents provided above** - It contains:

- **Overview**: Hardware → M4L translation with MIDI and Live parameter outputs
- **Architecture**: Hybrid signal-rate (timing-critical) + message-rate (config)
- **v1 Scope**: 2 tracks, 8 stages, full gate system, 10 playback orders, 4 MOD lanes, quantizer with 49 factory + 20 user scales
- **Data Model**: Complete specification of all parameters including:
  - Global settings (MIDI channel, total pulses, root note, scale select, etc.)
  - Shared stage controls (pitch slider, pulse count, gate type)
  - Per-track parameters (direction, transpose, slider octaves, gate overrides, etc.)
  - Per-stage per-track parameters (slide toggle, skip, pitch override, accumulator)
  - Modulation lanes with independent sequencing
  - **383 total parameters** (30-40 Tier 1 automated, ~350 Tier 2 stored, ~30 Tier 3 hidden)

- **Signal-Rate Architecture**: 
  - `phasor~ @lock 1` for master clock
  - `stepcounter~`, `stepdiv~`, `stepfun~` for step sequencing
  - `gen.codebox~` for accumulator, probability, gate generation
  - `schedule` → `midiformat` → `midiout` for MIDI output with scheduler precision

- **Development Stages** (11 stages total):
  1. Project skeleton, clock engine, minimal UI
  2. Gate system and note output
  3. Quantizer and scale system
  4. Playback orders and ratcheting
  5. Slide/portamento and per-stage lanes
  6. Track 2 modulation output
  7. Modulation system (MOD lanes, CTRL, AUX)
  8. Full UI with tabs
  9. Preset system (16 presets, 2 banks of 8)
  10. Auxiliary output lane and MOD outputs
  11. Polish and edge cases

- **Appendices**:
  - Scale database (49 factory scales in 7 banks)
  - Playback order quick reference (10 v1 orders)
  - Parameter count estimate
  - File structure
  - Critical implementation notes
  - Pitch pipeline (10-step process)
  - Accumulator gate type interaction table

### 5. tools/validate_maxpat.py - Complete Tool Reference

This is a comprehensive 2093-line Python validator that:

**Key Features:**
- Validates `.maxpat` and `.amxd` files
- Checks structural integrity, graph topology, signal/message compatibility
- M4L-specific validation (parameter registry, plugin~/plugout~, live.* objects)
- ~300+ known object signatures with inlet/outlet counts
- Dynamic resolvers for argument-dependent objects (trigger, route, sel, gate, pack, unpack, etc.)
- Detects:
  - Missing required fields
  - Duplicate object IDs
  - Outlet type mismatches
  - Invalid patchline references
  - Index out-of-bounds errors
  - Signal-to-message incompatibilities
  - Message-domain cycles
  - Orphaned objects
  - Fan-out missing order fields
  - Subpatcher port mismatches
  - gen~ namespace issues
  - Recursion depth > 5
  - Multiple loadbangs
  - live.observer without deferlow
  - Duplicate parameter longnames
  - Max 9-only objects in Max 8 patches
  - And ~30+ more checks

**Exit Codes:**
- 0 = no errors (PASS)
- 1 = errors found (FAIL)
- 2 = usage error

**Severity Levels:**
- ERROR — patch will not work correctly
- WARNING — likely a bug but could be intentional
- INFO — convention violation that won't break anything

### 6. Key Implementation Insights

**Current State of Metropolix.maxpat:**
1. The patch is at an **early prototype/skeleton stage** (862 lines, basic structure)
2. Contains the minimal framework for a MIDI effect device
3. Has `midiin` and `midiout` objects (MIDI effect template)
4. Has presentation mode enabled
5. Awaits full implementation of the 11 development stages outlined in the plan

**v8 JavaScript Approach:**
- Extremely minimal (only 65 lines)
- Used only for initialization and pitch/pulse conversion
- NOT in the timing-critical path
- Follows the principle: "v8 runs ONLY in the low-priority thread"

**Architecture Validation Tool:**
- The `validate_maxpat.py` tool is **comprehensive and production-ready**
- Can catch the vast majority of patch structure issues
- Essential for pre-push verification (per CLAUDE.md requirements)
- 2093 lines with extensive test coverage for Max 9 features

---

## Summary

The Metropolix implementation is at the **specification + skeleton phase**:
- **Complete specification**: 1089-line implementation plan with all 11 development stages
- **Minimal patch skeleton**: 862-line `.maxpat` with MIDI device template
- **Minimal v8 code**: 65-line config manager for initialization
- **Production validator**: 2093-line `validate_maxpat.py` tool ready for CI checks

The codebase is well-documented, architecturally sound, and ready for staged development starting with Stage 1 (Project Skeleton, Clock Engine, Minimal UI).

1→# Metropolix Max4Live MIDI Device - Implementation Plan (v2)
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→Faithful recreation of the Intellijel Metropolix 8-stage pitch and gate sequencer as a **Max4Live MIDI Effect** targeting **Max 9 / Live 12**. The device outputs MIDI on TRK1 and exposes TRK2 as modulation output parameters for the user to map freely within their Ableton Live project.
     6→
     7→### Hardware → M4L Translation
     8→
     9→The hardware Metropolix operates in the eurorack ecosystem with control voltages. This M4L implementation translates everything into the MIDI and Live parameter domains:
    10→
    11→| Metropolix (Hardware)    | M4L Implementation                                                                                   |
    12→| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    13→| 1V/Oct pitch CV          | MIDI note number (0-127) via `midiout`                                                               |
    14→| Gate CV (0V / 5V)        | MIDI note-on / note-off                                                                              |
    15→| Velocity CV              | MIDI velocity (1-127)                                                                                |
    16→| TRK2 pitch/gate/velocity | Normalized `live.dial` parameters (0.0-1.0) — modulation outputs the user maps to any Live parameter |
    17→| CV Lane output (±5V)     | Normalized `live.dial` parameter (0.0-1.0) — user maps externally                                    |
    18→| MOD OUT A / OUT B (±5V)  | Normalized `live.dial` parameters (0.0-1.0) — user maps externally                                   |
    19→| AUX inputs (±5V)         | `live.dial` parameters (0.0-1.0) — external sources map into these                                   |
    20→| CTRL knobs               | `live.dial` parameters — internal routing + user maps externally                                     |
    21→
    22→**There is no concept of control voltage in this implementation.** All modulation sources and outputs are normalized values (0.0-1.0) exposed as automatable Live parameters.
    23→
    24→### Architecture Constraints
    25→
    26→- **TRK1**: Direct MIDI output via `midiout` (pitch, velocity, gate on/off)
    27→- **TRK2**: Modulation output — pitch, velocity, and gate are exposed as `live.dial` parameters that the user maps to any target in their project. No `live.remote~` takeover of remote parameters. TRK2 runs the same sequencer engine as TRK1 but its output is parameter values, not MIDI notes.
    28→- **Transport**: Syncs to Live's transport via `phasor~ @lock 1` for sample-accurate timing. `plugsync~` for transport state. `transport` object for UI display only.
    29→- **Timing-critical path**: Signal-rate objects only (`phasor~`, `stepcounter~`, `stepdiv~`, `stepfun~`, `gen.codebox~`). **v8 JavaScript is NOT used in the timing-critical path** — it runs only in the low-priority thread. v8 is used for configuration, precomputation, preset management, and UI logic only.
    30→- **MIDI output**: Routed through Max 9's `schedule` object for scheduler-thread timing precision.
    31→- **Loopy Mode**: Explicitly excluded from this implementation.
    32→- **Target**: Max 9 features (v8, array._, gen.codebox~, stepfun~/stepdiv~/stepcounter~, string._) are preferred per CLAUDE.md.
    33→- **Modulation I/O**: All modulation outputs are exposed as `live.dial` parameters for user mapping. **v1 does not use `live.modulate~` internally**; if added later, it is a v2 feature and must use bipolar scaling.
    34→
    35→### v1 Scope
    36→
    37→**Included in v1:**
    38→
    39→- 2 tracks with independent stepping (shared base controls, per-track interpretation)
    40→- 8 stages with all per-stage lanes
    41→- Full gate system (4 types + ratchets)
    42→- Quantizer with 49 factory scales + 20 user scales
    43→- 10 playback orders (Linear, Ping Pong, Pendulum, Random, Shuffle, Brownian, Converge, Diverge, Pedal Point, Hopscotch)
    44→- 4 MOD lanes (independent sequencers)
    45→- 2 CTRL knobs + 3 AUX inputs
    46→- Accumulator (full implementation)
    47→- Slide/portamento (3 types)
    48→- 16 presets (2 banks of 8)
    49→- Tabbed UI faithful to hardware layout
    50→
    51→**Deferred to v2:**
    52→
    53→- Remaining 10 playback orders
    54→- 4 additional MOD lanes (total 8)
    55→- Preset chains
    56→- 64 presets (8 banks of 8)
    57→- 80 additional user scales (total 100)
    58→- Full OUT A/B flexible output types
    59→- Push integration / live.banks
    60→- Preset interpolation
    61→
    62→---
    63→
    64→## Data Model
    65→
    66→Based on the Metropolix "What's Stored Where" hierarchy (manual pp. 134-138).
    67→
    68→### Global Settings (Not Per-Preset)
    69→
    70→| Parameter               | Range                      | Notes                                                        |
    71→| ----------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
    72→| MIDI Channel TRK1       | 1-16                       | Channel for direct MIDI output                               |
    73→| Total Pulses            | — / 1-1024                 | Global pulse length; resets all tracks + MOD lanes when set  |
    74→| Root Note               | C-B                        | Global quantizer root                                        |
    75→| Scale Select            | 0-68                       | Index into scale bank (49 factory + 20 user for v1)          |
    76→| User Scales             | 20 scales (2 banks of 10)  | 12-bit bitmasks                                              |
    77→| Bottom Pitch            | C / Root                   | Whether slider bottom maps to C0 or to the current root note |
    78→| CTRL 1/2 Assignments    | Destination enum           | What the CTRL knobs control                                  |
    79→| AUX X/Y/Z Assignments   | Destination + Attenuverter | External modulation inputs                                   |
    80→| AUX X/Y/Z Attenuverters | -100 to +100               | Bipolar scaling                                              |
    81→
    82→### Shared Stage Controls (x8 stages — shared between TRK1 and TRK2)
    83→
    84→Like the hardware, both tracks share the same 8 base controls. Per-track parameters (Slider Octaves, Slider Direction, overrides) diverge from this shared base.
    85→
    86→| Parameter    | Range                  | Notes                                                                                  |
    87→| ------------ | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    88→| Pitch Slider | 0.0-1.0 (normalized)   | Shared physical slider — per-track interpretation via Slider Octaves, Slider Direction |
